0: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
1: And the earth was waste and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep: and the spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.
2: And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.
3: And God saw the light, that it was good: and God divided the light from the darkness.
4: And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. And there was evening and there was morning, one day.
5: And God said, Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters.
6: And God made the firmament, and divided the waters which were under the firmament from the waters which were above the firmament: and it was so.
7: And God called the firmament Heaven. And there was evening and there was morning, a second day.
8: And God said, Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear: and it was so.
9: And God called the dry land Earth; and the gathering together of the waters called he Seas: and God saw that it was good.
10: And God said, Let the earth put forth grass, herb yielding seed, and fruit tree bearing fruit after its kind, wherein is the seed thereof, upon the earth: and it was so.
11: And the earth brought forth grass, herb yielding seed after its kind, and tree bearing fruit, wherein is the seed thereof, after its kind: and God saw that it was good.
12: And there was evening and there was morning, a third day.
13: And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days and years:
14: and let them be for lights in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth: and it was so.
15: And God made the two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also.
16: And God set them in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth,
17: and to rule over the day and over the night, and to divide the light from the darkness: and God saw that it was good.
18: And there was evening and there was morning, a fourth day.
19: And God said, Let the waters bring forth abundantly the moving creature that hath life, and let fowl fly above the earth in the open firmament of heaven.
20: And God created the great sea-monsters, and every living creature that moveth, which the waters brought forth abundantly, after their kinds, and every winged fowl after its kind: and God saw that it was good.
21: And God blessed them, saying, Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas, and let fowl multiply in the earth.
22: And there was evening and there was morning, a fifth day.
23: And God said, Let the earth bring forth the living creature after its kind, cattle, and creeping thing, and beast of the earth after its kind: and it was so.
24: And God made the beast of the earth after its kind, and the cattle after their kind, and every thing that creepeth upon the ground after its kind: and God saw that it was good.
25: And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.
26: And God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.
27: And God blessed them: and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it; and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth.
28: And God said, Behold, I have given you every herb yielding seed, which is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree, in the which is the fruit of a tree yielding seed; to you it shall be for meat:
29: and to every beast of the earth, and to every fowl of the air, and to every thing that creepeth upon the earth, wherein there is life, I have given every green herb for meat: and it was so.
30: And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good. And there was evening and there was morning, the sixth day.
31: And the heaven and the earth were finished, and all the host of them.
32: And on the seventh day God finished his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made.
33: And God blessed the seventh day, and hallowed it: because that in it he rested from all his work which God had created and made.
34: These are the generations of the heaven and of the earth when they were created, in the day that the LORD God made earth and heaven.
35: And no plant of the field was yet in the earth, and no herb of the field had yet sprung up: for the LORD God had not caused it to rain upon the earth, and there was not a man to till the ground;
36: but there went up a mist from the earth, and watered the whole face of the ground.
37: And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
38: And the LORD God planted a garden eastward, in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed.
39: And out of the ground made the LORD God to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food; the tree of life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
40: And a river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from thence it was parted, and became four heads.
41: The name of the first is Pishon: that is it which compasseth the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold;
42: and the gold of that land is good: there is bdellium and the onyx stone.
43: And the name of the second river is Gihon: the same is it that compasseth the whole land of Cush.
44: And the name of the third river is Hiddekel: that is it which goeth in front of Assyria. And the fourth river is Euphrates.
45: And the LORD God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.
46: And the LORD God commanded the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat:
47: but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.
48: And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.
49: And out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field, and every fowl of the air; and brought them unto the man to see what he would call them: and whatsoever the man called every living creature, that was the name thereof.
50: And the man gave names to all cattle, and to the fowl of the air, and to every beast of the field; but for man there was not found an help meet for him.
51: And the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon the man, and he slept; and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof:
52: and the rib, which the LORD God had taken from the man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.
53: And the man said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.
54: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.
55: And they were both naked, the man and his wife, and were not ashamed.
56: Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the LORD God had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of any tree of the garden?
57: And the woman said unto the serpent, Of the fruit of the trees of the garden we may eat:
58: but of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, God hath said, Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die.
60: for God doth know that in the day ye eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as God, knowing good and evil.
61: And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes, and that the tree was to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat; and she gave also unto her husband with her, and he did eat.
62: And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons.
63: And they heard the voice of the LORD God walking in the garden in the cool of the day: and the man and his wife hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God amongst the trees of the garden.
64: And the LORD God called unto the man, and said unto him, Where art thou?
65: And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; and I hid myself.
66: And he said, Who told thee that thou wast naked? Hast thou eaten of the tree, whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldest not eat?
67: And the man said, The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat.
68: And the LORD God said unto the woman, What is this thou hast done? And the woman said, The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.
69: And the LORD God said unto the serpent, Because thou hast done this, cursed art thou above all cattle, and above every beast of the field; upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life:
70: and I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed: it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.
71: Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.
72: And unto Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in toil shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life;
73: thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field;
74: in the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.
75: And the man called his wife’s name Eve; because she was the mother of all living.
76: And the LORD God made for Adam and for his wife coats of skins, and clothed them.
77: And the LORD God said, Behold, the man is become as one of us, to know good and evil; and now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever:
78: therefore the LORD God sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from whence he was taken.
79: So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden the Cherubim, and the flame of a sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.
80: And the man knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man with the help of the LORD.
81: And again she bare his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.
82: And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the LORD.
83: And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the LORD had respect unto Abel and to his offering:
84: but unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.
85: And the LORD said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen?
86: If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin coucheth at the door: and unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.
87: And Cain told Abel his brother. And it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.
88: And the LORD said unto Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? And he said, I know not: am I my brother’s keeper?
89: And he said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth unto me from the ground.
90: And now cursed art thou from the ground, which hath opened her mouth to receive thy brother’s blood from thy hand;
91: when thou tillest the ground, it shall not henceforth yield unto thee her strength; a fugitive and a wanderer shalt thou be in the earth.
92: And Cain said unto the LORD, My punishment is greater than I can bear.
93: Behold, thou hast driven me out this day from the face of the ground; and from thy face shall I be hid; and I shall be a fugitive and a wanderer in the earth; and it shall come to pass, that whosoever findeth me shall slay me.
94: And the LORD said unto him, Therefore whosoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold. And the LORD appointed a sign for Cain, lest any finding him should smite him.
95: And Cain went out from the presence of the LORD, and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden.
96: And Cain knew his wife; and she conceived, and bare Enoch: and he builded a city, and called the name of the city, after the name of his son, Enoch.
97: And unto Enoch was born Irad: and Irad begat Mehujael: and Mehujael begat Methushael: and Methushael begat Lamech.
98: And Lamech took unto him two wives: the name of the one was Adah, and the name of the other Zillah.
99: And Adah bare Jabal: he was the father of such as dwell in tents and have cattle.
100: And his brother’s name was Jubal: he was the father of all such as handle the harp and pipe.
101: And Zillah, she also bare Tubal-cain, the forger of every cutting instrument of brass and iron: and the sister of Tubal-cain was Naamah.
102: And Lamech said unto his wives: Adah and Zillah, hear my voice; Ye wives of Lamech, hearken unto my speech: For I have slain a man for wounding me, And a young man for bruising me:
103: If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, Truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold.
104: And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For, said she, God hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel; for Cain slew him.
105: And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enosh: then began men to call upon the name of the LORD.
106: This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made he him;
108: And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth:
109: and the days of Adam after he begat Seth were eight hundred years: and he begat sons and daughters.
110: And all the days that Adam lived were nine hundred and thirty years: and he died.
111: And Seth lived an hundred and five years, and begat Enosh:
112: and Seth lived after he begat Enosh eight hundred and seven years, and begat sons and daughters:
113: and all the days of Seth were nine hundred and twelve years: and he died.
114: And Enosh lived ninety years, and begat Kenan:
115: and Enosh lived after he begat Kenan eight hundred and fifteen years, and begat sons and daughters:
117: And Kenan lived seventy years, and begat Mahalalel:
118: and Kenan lived after he begat Mahalalel eight hundred and forty years, and begat sons and daughters:
119: and all the days of Kenan were nine hundred and ten years: and he died.
120: And Mahalalel lived sixty and five years, and begat Jared:
126: And Enoch lived sixty and five years, and begat Methuselah:
127: and Enoch walked with God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters:
130: And Methuselah lived an hundred eighty and seven years, and begat Lamech:
134: and he called his name Noah, saying, This same shall comfort us for our work and for the toil of our hands, because of the ground which the LORD hath cursed.
137: And Noah was five hundred years old: and Noah begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
139: that the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all that they chose.
140: And the LORD said, My spirit shall not strive with man for ever, for that he also is flesh: yet shall his days be an hundred and twenty years.
141: The Nephilim were in the earth in those days, and also after that, when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them: the same were the mighty men which were of old, the men of renown.
142: And the LORD saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.
143: And it repented the LORD that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him at his heart.
144: And the LORD said, I will destroy man whom I have created from the face of the ground; both man, and beast, and creeping thing, and fowl of the air; for it repeateth me that I have made them.
145: But Noah found grace in the eyes of the LORD.
146: These are the generations of Noah. Noah was a righteous man, and perfect in his generations: Noah walked with God.
148: And the earth was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence.
149: And God saw the earth, and, behold, it was corrupt; for all flesh had corrupted his way upon the earth.
150: And God said unto Noah, The end of all flesh is come before me; for the earth is filled with violence through them; and, behold, I will destroy them with the earth.
151: Make thee an ark of gopher wood; rooms shalt thou make in the ark, and shalt pitch it within and without with pitch.
152: And this is how thou shalt make it: the length of the ark three hundred cubits, the breadth of it fifty cubits, and the height of it thirty cubits.
153: A light shalt thou make to the ark, and to a cubit shalt thou finish it upward; and the door of the ark shalt thou set in the side thereof; with lower, second, and third stories shalt thou make it.
154: And I, behold, I do bring the flood of waters upon the earth, to destroy all flesh, wherein is the breath of life, from under heaven; every thing that is in the earth shall die.
155: But I will establish my covenant with thee; and thou shalt come into the ark, thou, and thy sons, and thy wife, and thy sons’ wives with thee.
156: And of every living thing of all flesh, two of every sort shalt thou bring into the ark, to keep them alive with thee; they shall be male and female.
158: And take thou unto thee of all food that is eaten, and gather it to thee; and it shall be for food for thee, and for them.
159: Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he.
160: And the LORD said unto Noah, Come thou and all thy house into the ark; for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation.
161: Of every clean beast thou shalt take to thee seven and seven, the male and his female; and of the beasts that are not clean two, the male and his female;
163: For yet seven days, and I will cause it to rain upon the earth forty days and forty nights; and every living thing that I have made will I destroy from off the face of the ground.
165: And Noah was six hundred years old when the flood of waters was upon the earth.
167: Of clean beasts, and of beasts that are not clean, and of fowls, and of every thing that creepeth upon the ground,
170: In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on the same day were all the fountains of the great deep broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened.
172: In the selfsame day entered Noah, and Shem, and Ham, and Japheth, the sons of Noah, and Noah’s wife, and the three wives of his sons with them, into the ark;
173: they, and every beast after its kind, and all the cattle after their kind, and every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth after its kind, and every fowl after its kind, every bird of every sort.
175: And they that went in, went in male and female of all flesh, as God commanded him: and the LORD shut him in.
176: And the flood was forty days upon the earth; and the waters increased, and bare up the ark, and it was lift up above the earth.
177: And the waters prevailed, and increased greatly upon the earth; and the ark went upon the face of the waters.
178: And the waters prevailed exceedingly upon the earth; and all the high mountains that were under the whole heaven were covered.
179: Fifteen cubits upward did the waters prevail; and the mountains were covered.
181: all in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life, of all that was in the dry land, died.
182: And every living thing was destroyed which was upon the face of the ground, both man, and cattle, and creeping thing, and fowl of the heaven; and they were destroyed from the earth: and Noah only was left, and they that were with him in the ark.
184: And God remembered Noah, and every living thing, and all the cattle that were with him in the ark: and God made a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters assuaged;
185: the fountains also of the deep and the windows of heaven were stopped, and the rain from heaven was restrained;
186: and the waters returned from off the earth continually: and after the end of an hundred and fifty days the waters decreased.
187: And the ark rested in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, upon the mountains of Ararat.
188: And the waters decreased continually until the tenth month: in the tenth month, on the first day of the month, were the tops of the mountains seen.
189: And it came to pass at the end of forty days, that Noah opened the window of the ark which he had made:
190: and he sent forth a raven, and it went forth to and fro, until the waters were dried up from off the earth.
191: And he sent forth a dove from him, to see if the waters were abated from off the face of the ground;
192: but the dove found no rest for the sole of her foot, and she returned unto him to the ark, for the waters were on the face of the whole earth: and he put forth his hand, and took her, and brought her in unto him into the ark.
193: And he stayed yet other seven days; and again he sent forth the dove out of the ark;
194: and the dove came in to him at eventide; and, lo, in her mouth an olive leaf pluckt off: so Noah knew that the waters were abated from off the earth.
196: And it came to pass in the six hundred and first year, in the first month, the first day of the month, the waters were dried up from off the earth: and Noah removed the covering of the ark, and looked, and, behold, the face of the ground was dried.
197: And in the second month, on the seven and twentieth day of the month, was the earth dry.
198: And God spake unto Noah, saying,
200: Bring forth with thee every living thing that is with thee of all flesh, both fowl, and cattle, and every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth; that they may breed abundantly in the earth, and be fruitful, and multiply upon the earth.
202: every beast, every creeping thing, and every fowl, whatsoever moveth upon the earth, after their families, went forth out of the ark.
203: And Noah builded an altar unto the LORD; and took of every clean beast, and of every clean fowl, and offered burnt offerings on the altar.
204: And the LORD smelled the sweet savour; and the LORD said in his heart, I will not again curse the ground any more for man’s sake, for that the imagination of man’s heart is evil from his youth; neither will I again smite any more every thing living, as I have done.
205: While the earth remaineth, seedtime and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night shall not cease.
207: And the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth, and upon every fowl of the air; with all wherewith the ground teemeth, and all the fishes of the sea, into your hand are they delivered.
208: Every moving thing that liveth shall be food for you; as the green herb have I given you all.
210: And surely your blood, the blood of your lives, will I require; at the hand of every beast will I require it: and at the hand of man, even at the hand of every man’s brother, will I require the life of man.
211: Whoso sheddeth man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of God made he man.
212: And you, be ye fruitful, and multiply; bring forth abundantly in the earth, and multiply therein.
216: And I will establish my covenant with you; neither shall all flesh be cut off any more by the waters of the flood; neither shall there any more be a flood to destroy the earth.
217: And God said, This is the token of the covenant which I make between me and you and every living creature that is with you, for perpetual generations:
218: I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth.
220: and I will remember my covenant, which is between me and you and every living creature of all flesh; and the waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh.
221: And the bow shall be in the cloud; and I will look upon it, that I may remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is upon the earth.
222: And God said unto Noah, This is the token of the covenant which I have established between me and all flesh that is upon the earth.
223: And the sons of Noah, that went forth of the ark, were Shem, and Ham, and Japheth: and Ham is the father of Canaan.
224: These three were the sons of Noah: and of these was the whole earth overspread.
225: And Noah began to be an husbandman, and planted a vineyard:
226: and he drank of the wine, and was drunken; and he was uncovered within his tent.
227: And Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father, and told his two brethren without.
228: And Shem and Japheth took a garment, and laid it upon both their shoulders, and went backward, and covered the nakedness of their father; and their faces were backward, and they saw not their father’s nakedness.
229: And Noah awoke from his wine, and knew what his youngest son had done unto him.
230: And he said, Cursed be Canaan; A servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren.
232: God enlarge Japheth, And let him dwell in the tents of Shem; And let Canaan be his servant.
236: The sons of Japheth; Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Javan, and Tubal, and Meshech, and Tiras.
237: And the sons of Gomer; Ashkenaz, and Riphath, and Togarmah.
238: And the sons of Javan; Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
239: Of these were the isles of the nations divided in their lands, every one after his tongue; after their families, in their nations.
240: And the sons of Ham; Cush, and Mizraim, and Put, and Canaan.
241: And the sons of Cush; Seba, and Havilah, and Sabtah, and Raamah, and Sabteca: and the sons of Raamah; Sheba, and Dedan.
242: And Cush begat Nimrod: he began to be a mighty one in the earth.
243: He was a mighty hunter before the LORD: wherefore it is said, Like Nimrod a mighty hunter before the LORD.
244: And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
245: Out of that land he went forth into Assyria, and builded Nineveh, and Rehoboth-Ir, and Calah,
246: and Resen between Nineveh and Calah (the same is the great city).
247: And Mizraim begat Ludim, and Anamim, and Lehabim, and Naphtuhim,
248: and Pathrusim, and Casluhim (whence went forth the Philistines), and Caphtorim.
249: And Canaan begat Zidon his firstborn, and Heth;
250: and the Jebusite, and the Amorite, and the Girgashite;
251: and the Hivite, and the Arkite, and the Sinite;
252: and the Arvadite, and the Zemarite, and the Hamathite: and afterward were the families of the Canaanite spread abroad.
253: And the border of the Canaanite was from Zidon, as thou goest toward Gerar, unto Gaza; as thou goest toward Sodom and Gomorrah and Admah and Zeboiim, unto Lasha.
254: These are the sons of Ham, after their families, after their tongues, in their lands, in their nations.
255: And unto Shem, the father of all the children of Eber, the elder brother of Japheth, to him also were children born.
256: The sons of Shem; Elam, and Asshur, and Arpachshad, and Lud, and Aram.
257: And the sons of Aram; Uz, and Hul, and Gether, and Mash.
258: And Arpachshad begat Shelah; and Shelah begat Eber.
259: And unto Eber were born two sons: the name of the one was Peleg; for in his days was the earth divided; and his brother’s name was Joktan.
260: And Joktan begat Almodad, and Sheleph, and Hazarmaveth, and Jerah;
261: and Hadoram, and Uzal, and Diklah;
262: and Obal, and Abimael, and Sheba;
263: and Ophir, and Havilah, and Jobab: all these were the sons of Joktan.
264: And their dwelling was from Mesha, as thou goest toward Sephar, the mountain of the east.
267: And the whole earth was of one language and of one speech.
268: And it came to pass, as they journeyed east, that they found a plain in the land of Shinar; and they dwelt there.
269: And they said one to another, Go to, let us make brick, and burn them throughly. And they had brick for stone, and slime had they for mortar.
270: And they said, Go to, let us build us a city, and a tower, whose top may reach unto heaven, and let us make us a name; lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth.
271: And the LORD came down to see the city and the tower, which the children of men builded.
272: And the LORD said, Behold, they are one people, and they have all one language; and this is what they begin to do: and now nothing will be withholden from them, which they purpose to do.
273: Go to, let us go down, and there confound their language, that they may not understand one another’s speech.
275: Therefore was the name of it called Babel; because the LORD did there confound the language of all the earth: and from thence did the LORD scatter them abroad upon the face of all the earth.
284: And Peleg lived thirty years, and begat Reu:
286: And Reu lived two and thirty years, and begat Serug:
288: And Serug lived thirty years, and begat Nahor:
290: And Nahor lived nine and twenty years, and begat Terah:
291: and Nahor lived after he begat Terah an hundred and nineteen years, and begat sons and daughters.
292: And Terah lived seventy years, and begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran.

417: And as for Ishmael, I have heard thee: behold, I have blessed him, and will make him fruitful, and will multiply him exceedingly; twelve princes shall he beget, and I will make him a great nation.

441: And the LORD said, Shall I hide from Abraham that which I do;

444: And the LORD said, Because the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah is great, and because their sin is very grievous;

447: And Abraham drew near, and said, Wilt thou consume the righteous with the wicked?
448: Peradventure there be fifty righteous within the city: wilt thou consume and not spare the place for the fifty righteous that are therein?
450: And the LORD said, If I find in Sodom fifty righteous within the city, then I will spare all the place for their sake.
451: And Abraham answered and said, Behold now, I have taken upon me to speak unto the Lord, which am but dust and ashes:
452: peradventure there shall lack five of the fifty righteous: wilt thou destroy all the city for lack of five? And he said, I will not destroy it, if I find there forty and five.
453: And he spake unto him yet again, and said, Peradventure there shall be forty found there. And he said, I will not do it for the forty’s sake.

455: And he said, Behold now, I have taken upon me to speak unto the Lord: peradventure there shall be twenty found there. And he said, I will not destroy it for the twenty’s sake.
456: And he said, Oh let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak yet but this once: peradventure ten shall be found there. And he said, I will not destroy it for the ten’s sake.

458: And the two angels came to Sodom at even; and Lot sat in the gate of Sodom: and Lot saw them, and rose up to meet them; and he bowed himself with his face to the earth;

464: And he said, I pray you, my brethren, do not so wickedly.

519: And Sarah said, God hath made me to laugh; every one that heareth will laugh with me.

1969: And it came to pass, that on the sixth day they gathered twice as much bread, two omers for each one: and all the rulers of the congregation came and told Moses.
1970: And he said unto them, This is that which the LORD hath spoken, Tomorrow is a solemn rest, a holy sabbath unto the LORD: bake that which ye will bake, and seethe that which ye will seethe; and all that remaineth over lay up for you to be kept until the morning.
1971: And they laid it up till the morning, as Moses bade: and it did not stink, neither was there any worm therein.
1978: And the house of Israel called the name thereof Manna: and it was like coriander seed, white; and the taste of it was like wafers made with honey.
1979: And Moses said, This is the thing which the LORD hath commanded, Let an omerful of it be kept for your generations; that they may see the bread wherewith I fed you in the wilderness, when I brought you forth from the land of Egypt.
1980: And Moses said unto Aaron, Take a pot, and put an omerful of manna therein, and lay it up before the LORD, to be kept for your generations.
1981: As the LORD commanded Moses, so Aaron laid it up before the Testimony, to be kept.
1982: And the children of Israel did eat the manna forty years, until they came to a land inhabited; they did eat the manna, until they came unto the borders of the land of Canaan.
1984: And all the congregation of the children of Israel journeyed from the wilderness of Sin, by their journeys, according to the commandment of the LORD, and pitched in Rephidim: and there was no water for the people to drink.
1985: Wherefore the people strove with Moses, and said, Give us water that we may drink. And Moses said unto them, Why strive ye with me? wherefore do ye tempt the LORD?
1986: And the people thirsted there for water; and the people murmured against Moses, and said, Wherefore hast thou brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our cattle with thirst?
1987: And Moses cried unto the LORD, saying, What shall I do unto this people? they be almost ready to stone me.
1988: And the LORD said unto Moses, Pass on before the people, and take with thee of the elders of Israel; and thy rod, wherewith thou smotest the river, take in thine hand, and go.
1989: Behold, I will stand before thee there upon the rock in Horeb; and thou shalt smite the rock, and there shall come water out of it, that the people may drink. And Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel.
1990: And he called the name of the place Massah, and Meribah, because of the striving of the children of Israel, and because they tempted the LORD, saying, Is the LORD among us, or not?
1991: Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim.
1992: And Moses said unto Joshua, Choose us out men, and go out, fight with Amalek: tomorrow I will stand on the top of the hill with the rod of God in mine hand.
1993: So Joshua did as Moses had said to him, and fought with Amalek: and Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
1995: But Moses’ hands were heavy; and they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat thereon; and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side; and his hands were steady until the going down of the sun.
1997: And the LORD said unto Moses, Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: that I will utterly blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven.
